title: Daily Caffeine Load vs Curfew
dataSources: Beanconqueror brews (`beanconqueror:brew`), Acaia brew sessions (`acaia:brew`), Decent Espresso shots (`decent:shot`), Brewfather coffee recipes (`brewfather:coffee`), and tea-timer sessions (`teatimer:session`).
app: Beanconqueror brews, Acaia scale sessions, Decent Espresso shot telemetry, Brewfather coffee recipes, and tea-timer app exports forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
(index=personal sourcetype=beanconqueror:brew OR sourcetype=decent:shot OR sourcetype=teatimer:session)
| eval caffeine_mg=coalesce(caffeine_mg,estimated_caffeine_mg,0)
| eval late_caffeine_mg=if(date_hour>=15,caffeine_mg,0)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(caffeine_mg) as total_caffeine_mg, sum(late_caffeine_mg) as late_caffeine_mg by _time
| eval status=if(late_caffeine_mg>100,"sleep risk","okay")
| sort - _time
description: Adds up total and late-day caffeine intake so you can see when the afternoon cutoff has been blown.
value: A caffeine curfew is easier to keep when it is visible as data instead of remembered fuzzily the next morning.
implementation: Normalize caffeine estimates across coffee and tea events and schedule a daily check after your personal cutoff time.
visualization: Daily column chart for total and late caffeine with a threshold line.
grandmaExplanation: It watches how much caffeine you had each day and whether too much of it arrived late enough to bother sleep.
